sentences.text: The holotype is a partial skeleton featuring a mostly complete skull, lower jaws, and the front section of the body.
Its name means 'Cañadón Asfalto Formation hunter,' directly referencing the specific rock layer where the fossils were found.
A technician named Leandro Canesa found the skeleton in 2002 near Cerro Condor.
Preparing the fossil required five years because the surrounding stone matrix was extremely hard.
Oliver Rauhut and Diego Pol formally named and described the species Asfaltovenator vialidadi in 2019.
This large theropod possessed a skull measuring 75 to 80 cm and a total body length estimated at 7 to 8 meters.
Its premaxillary teeth show large serrations on the rear edge but only tiny serrations on the front edge.
Fossils were found in the Chacritas Member, which consists of lake and river deposits.
The lake environment where it lived, known as the Chacritas Paleolake, was likely shallow, saline, or hypersaline.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Asfaltovenator as the most basal allosauroid and Megalosauroidea as a paraphyletic grade leading to Allosauroidea.
The genus Asfaltovenator belongs to the parent group Allosauroidea.

Asfaltovenator lived during the Middle Toarcian of the Lower Jurassic in the Cañadón Asfalto Formation of Chubut Province, Argentina, although the holotype specimen was found in a layer dating from the Late Toarcian to the Bajocian.
The animal lived between 180.4 and 168.6 million years ago during the Toarcian to Bajocian stages.
In 2024, Andrea Cau proposed that Asfaltovenator belongs within Megalosauroidea as a sister taxon to Sciurumimus or within a larger stem group.
